title: Ensemble Simulations on Leadership Computing Systems
problem: Large HPC system users spend significant time on tedious scheduling and complex computational workflow design for scientific applications. Ensemble workflow tools require careful porting and optimization to efficiently leverage modern leadership computing systems.
motivation: Workflow management tools can accelerate HPC-enabled scientific discovery and increase research impact by automating job scheduling and coordination.
method: The research adapts Radical-Cybertools—a tool that manages ensembles (collections of related computational jobs that run together)—to work on Summit and Frontier supercomputers. It uses a pilot scheduler that divides the supercomputer's resources among multiple jobs simultaneously, rather than running one massive job at a time. The team tests this on three scientific applications: Chroma, NAMD, and LAMMPS, optimizing their performance. They develop data management strategies that follow the facility's operational constraints.
key_novelty: It enables production ensemble workflow management on leadership-class supercomputers by solving the integration challenges that arise when coordinating multiple related computational jobs alongside large-scale scientific applications.
contributions: Empirical evaluation of Radical-Cybertools on Summit and Frontier leadership computing systems
Successful porting and optimization of ensemble workflows for three scientific domains (Chroma, NAMD, LAMMPS)
Identification of technical challenges and developed solutions for workflow tool integration with large HPC systems
Data management strategies and OLCF operational policies for ensemble workflow execution
limitations: The paper discusses intrinsic limitations of coupling workflow tools to large HPC systems but does not provide detailed quantitative scalability analysis or performance characterization.
